newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Annan urged to back Malaysian in $25mln libel case.
newsitem.headline: Annan urged to back Malaysian in $25mln libel case.

text.p: U.N. human rights investigators have closed ranks around a Malaysian colleague, urging U.N. chief Kofi Annan to take further steps to protect his immunity from a $25 million libel suit, a U.N. statement said on Friday.
In a joint letter, the 30 experts argued the immunity from legal process granted to U.N. specialists under a 1946 convention had been undermined by the Malaysian courts.

A Malaysian High Court last month allowed a libel suit by two Malaysian companies to proceed against Param Cumaraswamy, a Malaysian lawyer who serves as U.N. special rapporteur (investigator) on the Independence of Judges and Lawyers.

MBf Capital Bhd and MBf Northern Securities Sdn Bhd alleged Cumaraswamy had defamed them in an article published in the November 1995 issue of the International Commercial Litigation magazine, a London-based publication. In the article, he was quoted as saying he was investigating complaints that businessmen were manipulating the Malaysian judicial system.
U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights Ralph Zacklin said in the statement that the world body regarded the matter with the "utmost seriousness and urgency".

Annan already waded into the lawsuit last March, submitting a certificate to the court asserting Cumaraswamy enjoyed the protections provided under the Convention on Privileges and Immunities of the United Nations.
The rapporteurs -- who investigate allegations in countries including Burma, Iran and Nigeria -- wrote Annan "asking for a further affirmation of the immunity of the Special Rapporteurs".

"Threatening the immunity of one expert constitutes an attack on the entire system and institution of the United Nations special (human rights) procedures and mechanisms," the statement quoted the letter as saying.
It was signed by Paulo Sergio Pinheiro, special rapporteur on Burundi, who currently serves as chairman of the group.
The letter stopped short of calls by some non-governmental organisations urging Annan to immediately bring the case of Cumaraswamy's immunity to the International Court of Justice.
On June 28, Judicial Commissioner Zainun Ali dismissed with costs Cumaraswamy's application to strike out the 60 million ringgit ($23.8 million) suit by the two firms.
She ordered him to file and serve his defence within 14 days, but said he could cite evidence at the trial to support his claim of immunity, according to Malaysia's New Sunday Times.
